headline: Meadows of Mayhem: National Council Awards Certification for Ignition-Resistant Native Overgrowth
deck: Local HOAs replace lawn regulations with ambitious vegetation mandates, promising ecological prestige amid smoldering chaos.
article:
The National Meadow Expansion Council has rolled out its Ignition-Resistant Native Overgrowth program, handing plaques to homeowners whose yards now function as vertical fuel stacks. The standard requires a continuous 14-inch ladder of dry stems from sidewalk to siding, turning every subdivision into a ready-made experiment.

Spokane’s HOA swapped its old grass rules for a 47-page density matrix that fines any exposed soil. Resident Betty Prospector summed up the new ethos: “Bare dirt is the real hazard.” Council director Morton Floret called the coming fire season “free validation data” for the next round of grants, then set a demonstration plot alight while praising its drought tolerance.

Residents in dry counties now compete to grow the tallest approved brush, while state planners redraw fire buffers around the very thickets they once cleared. The result is neighborhoods that look lush until the first spark arrives, at which point the awards and the flames arrive together.
author: Julius Blunderbuss, Senior Meadow Correspondent

oped.title: Certified Meadows: Proof That Fire Builds Character
oped.author: Horace Q. Flambé, Grand Poobah of Scorched Elegance and Certified Ember Enthusiast
oped.body: The Council’s ignition-resistant stamp is ecological progress, not a problem. These meadows burn with intent, clearing weak growth and raising property values through dramatic ash-scaping. Critics who see only chaos lack vision; a controlled burn is nature’s pruning shears. The true danger is straw hats on onlookers—fabric catches faster than native scrub. My neighbor’s plaid fedora has been a liability for years. Outlaw such millinery and we can enjoy prestige wildfires without distraction. Mandatory flame-retardant monocles would complete the look. Progress requires sacrifice, just not mine.

classifieds.text: Seeking certified native-overgrowth wrangler for 2026 HOA ignition audit. Must survive daily smolder checks and bring own asbestos overalls; pay in prestige points only.
For Sale: unused 2025 riding mower, mint condition. Owner forced into meadow certification; will throw in fire blanket and one slightly charred garden gnome.
Lost: my front porch swing and three rosebushes last Tuesday when the certified native patch went from smolder to full whoosh. Reward: one bucket of approved ignition-resistant seed mix.
Public Notice: Neighborly apology for the 'ecological prestige fire' that took out three mailboxes. HOA says it's fine now; please stop mailing the lawsuits.

panels.caption: Council inspector pins the plaque: 'Your HOA overgrowth is now officially ignition-resistant.'
Homeowner watches smoke curl from the back lot. Inspector: 'Minor self-thinning. Still certified.'
As the front porch ignites: 'We'll upgrade you to wildfire-premium next quarter.'

joke.setup: After the National Council stamped her meadow ignition-resistant, Mrs. Delgado nailed the plaque to her front gate and dared the county to find a single flammable blade.
joke.punchline: The August wildfire still torched the block in forty minutes, but at least the paperwork survived.

sponsor_ads.headline: Council-Approved Overgrowth in a Can
sponsor_ads.body: One spray of BlazeKelp turns your native meadow into ignition-resistant certified terrain before the next wind event; neighbors will whisper about your compliance.
sponsor_ads.tagline: May cause spontaneous Council visits and envious dirt patches.

sponsor_ads.headline: Honest Dirt: The Anti-Meadow
sponsor_ads.body: Replace your unruly overgrowth with sterile, non-flammable soil that the National Council cannot certify because it contains nothing to certify.

sponsor_ads.headline: Mayhem Insurance for Your Certified Meadow
sponsor_ads.body: If your ignition-resistant native plants still torch the subdivision, we pay the fine and replant with our own Council-approved seed mix.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Excludes acts of wind, drought, or overly ambitious native species.

sponsor_ads.headline: Meadow Certification or Else
sponsor_ads.body: Our mobile inspectors award instant ignition ratings while you watch; fail and we quietly seed your dirt with our competitors' flammable stock overnight.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Not affiliated with the National Council. Or so they claim.

stories.headline: Certified Native Seed Mandates Force Farmers to Replace Soy Rows With Fire-Safe Thistle
stories.deck: County extension offices report zero bushel yields but record pollen counts
stories.article: Inside certified districts, operators must devote 40 percent of acreage to ignition-resistant natives or lose subsidies. Combines sit idle; brush hogs now handle municipal contracts. Last season’s yields fell to 12 bushels per acre, so the Department of Agriculture created new forms for declaring meadows both habitat and zero-harvest zones.

stories.headline: Mower Manufacturers Pivot to 'Overgrowth Management' Mulchers After HOA Rule Changes
stories.deck: Quarterly earnings rise on sales of diesel-powered native-plant thinners
stories.article: Equipment makers rebranded mowers as selective-clearing tools and posted 38 percent revenue growth. Catalogs now list blades as “ecological compliance attachments.” The sector survived only after signing contracts with 1,200 HOAs that now charge meadow-maintenance fees instead of lawn fines.

stories.headline: Burglars Exploit Tall-Meadow Sightlines in Subdivisions Lacking Traditional Lawn Clearance
stories.deck: Police logs cite 27 percent rise in undetected property entries behind waist-high switchgrass
stories.article: Homeowners behind certified overgrowth report hidden windows and driveways. One association now requires reflective vests for evening walks. Deputies note unchanged response times, though recovered stolen goods increasingly include native-plant ID tags left at the scene.
